clue.text: Corrosion is found on most of range (i.e. cooking facility)

parts.note: rot is decay or corrosion

indicators.note: most of the word means its final letter is dropped, leaving all but one

parts.note: a range of things in sequence is a series

explanation.surface: A rusty oven, with the corrosion spread across most of the cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims SERIES to SERIE; 'i.e.' just links the wordplay to the definition, as in 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a roasting appliance with a turning spit, a piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Secure pawn in rank

indicators.note: in tells us the pawn's letter goes inside the word for rank

parts.note: rank in the sense of foul-smelling, as stale food can be
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player locking a pawn into position along a row of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a row on a chessboard, but it means smelly: STALE, with P put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To staple papers is to fasten them firmly together.

clue.text: Head child, high-flier

parts.note: an airman flies high, a pilot or aviator

explanation.surface: A list of a top pupil and an ambitious achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests an ambitious person, but it is read literally as someone who flies: an AIRMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The chairman is the person who leads a committee or board.

clue.text: Inclination to stash millions in trunk

indicators.note: to stash something is to hide it away inside, so millions go into the trunk

parts.note: a caber is a tree trunk tossed in Scottish Highland games
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to hide millions in a travelling chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests a storage chest, but it is the CABER, the tree trunk thrown at Scottish Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is a slight slope or tilt across a road surface.

clue.text: Liberal and last of Independents in the House

indicators.note: in places the conjunction and the final letter inside the word for the house

parts.note: one's house is one's home

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A Liberal and the last of the Independent members sitting in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' reads as the political party, but it means generous; 'the House' is a home, not Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome gift is a generous one, so the word can mean bountiful.

clue.text: Cut up, East European

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so reversed

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone sliced up an East European, a grisly report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East European' looks like one phrase, but 'East' gives E and 'European' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Poland is a European.

clue.text: Shaft of sun penetrating pool, maybe

indicators.note: penetrating means the sun's letter goes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a pot is a pool of money, as in the kitty in a card game
S is short for Sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A ray of sunshine breaking through into a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaft of sun' looks like one phrase for a sunbeam; 'Shaft' alone is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A post is an upright pole, much like a shaft.

clue.text: Rumpus in port with seaman at a card game

parts.note: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, England
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
loo is an old card game played for stakes

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out in a harbour town as a sailor plays cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hullabaloo is a noisy commotion or uproar.

clue.text: Cut up, East European Like a liberator, fighting mad, embraced by the French Revolutionary type

indicators.note: embraced by means the shuffled letters sit inside the French article

parts.note: le is the French masculine for the

indicators.note: mad suggests letters gone wild and rearranged

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A fighter frantic for freedom, hugged by French comrades in a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberator' sounds heroic, but to 'liberate' something is slang for stealing it, so the definition describes a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-fingered person is a thief, one who 'liberates' others' property.

clue.text: Tearing about lake, ruffling the surface

indicators.note: about means the word for tearing goes around the lake's letter

parts.note: ripping is tearing
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Something racing around a lake disturbs the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Rippling water has small waves moving across it.

clue.text: Inexpensive move at end of August

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

indicators.note: at end of points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cheap shift at the close of summer holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget used as an adjective describes cheap goods, as in budget airlines.

clue.text: Prize one ultimately gathers, retrospectively

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word one
looking back means the word for gathers is read backwards

parts.note: a crowd meets when it gathers

explanation.surface: Looking back, someone collects an award at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' looks like a noun for an award, but it is the verb: to value highly.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to value it highly, to hold it in high regard.

clue.text: Hat too brash in design

indicators.note: in design means the letters are laid out to a new pattern

explanation.surface: A hat that's a bit too loud in its styling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarboosh is a felt cap like a fez, worn in the Middle East.

clue.text: Set up home in county seat, at first

indicators.note: at first tells us the seat's word comes before the county's

parts.note: a settle is a wooden bench with a high back
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Moving into a house in a county town with its seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'county seat' looks like a county town; split it into two words. Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle down is to establish a stable home life.

clue.text: Harmony from the French playing pieces

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Harmony from the French playing pieces', has letters for LE and perhaps MEN but no fodder for the rest of RECONCILEMENT (RCONCIET); words appear lost in OCR and no reprint was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Harmony from the French playing pieces

clue.text: Red (primary)

definitions.meaning: a bright scarlet colour, from the robes of church princes

explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal is a deep scarlet colour, and also means chief or fundamental, as in cardinal sin.

clue.text: Exhibition certain to make appearance on TV?

parts.note: an expo is a large exhibition
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A show sure to get someone onto television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhibition' looks like the definition but gives EXPO; the question mark flags that being on TV is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is publicity, being seen by the public through the media.

clue.text: Wisdom or partiality, embracing Right?

indicators.note: embracing means the word for partiality wraps round the letter for right

parts.note: a leaning is a bias or preference

explanation.surface: A question of whether wisdom or bias leads one to embrace the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning means knowledge gained through study, close to wisdom.

clue.text: Demand expressed in unruly sit-ins

indicators.note: unruly suggests letters out of control and rearranged

explanation.surface: Protesters voice their demands at a disorderly occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand something firmly.

clue.text: Priest confused in row

parts.note: to addle is to muddle or confuse

explanation.surface: A muddled clergyman caught up in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it means to propel a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To paddle a canoe is to move it with oars or a blade, as rowing does.

clue.text: Stoops — product of Vikings, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the word is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: Danes are the people descended from the Viking raiders of Denmark

explanation.surface: Someone bends down to look at a relic of the Viking age.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, lowering oneself to do something.

clue.text: Receives grants

definitions.meaning: lets in, as a host welcomes a guest

explanation.definitionFit: To admit a visitor is to let them in, and to admit a point is to concede it.

clue.text: Dull English coin

parts.note: dim means dull, lacking brightness

explanation.surface: A tarnished old British penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English coin' looks like the definition, but 'English' gives E and the coin is American.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is the US ten-cent piece.

clue.text: East (Spade on Club in some cases) revokes

indicators.note: in puts the compass point and two card suits inside the coverings

parts.note: rinds are the protective skins or cases of fruit and cheese
E is the compass abbreviation for east
S is the abbreviation for spades in bridge
C is the abbreviation for clubs in bridge

explanation.surface: In a bridge game, East plays a spade on a club and then reneges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East' is a bridge player's seat in the surface, but here just E; 'on' links S before C.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law is to cancel or annul it.

clue.text: Agent aboard struggling with Mass

indicators.note: struggling means the letters writhe into a new order

explanation.surface: A secret agent on board fights with Mass, the setter's own pseudonym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges ABOARD with MASS; Mass is also this puzzle's setter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a diplomatic representative acting for a country.

clue.text: Creature with green tail of ET

parts.note: green means new and inexperienced

indicators.note: tail of takes the final letter of what follows

explanation.surface: A creature with green skin and the tail of the film alien ET.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' suggests colour, but means fresh or NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small amphibian, a kind of creature.
